title: Technical data
summary: Covers the sources of technical information for an installation: specifications, drawings, regulations, manufacturers' data and the client's needs.

sections.heading: Sources of technical information
paragraphs: An electrician draws on several sources of technical information when planning and installing.
bullets: Drawings (provide technical information on wiring systems)
BS 7671, the On-Site Guide and the Unite Union book
Guidance Notes (install in accordance with Regulations)

sections.heading: Specifications, drawings and diagrams
paragraphs: So that contractors can tender for work, detailed specifications, drawings and diagrams have to be produced. When pricing against other companies, everyone must use the same base for their final price.

Installation specifications give complete details of what is to be included in the installation, including plans. They give details of the equipment to be installed, where it is to be installed, sizes, etc.

sections.heading: Manufacturers' information and data
paragraphs: Manufacturers provide a wide range of information about their products in general and about specific equipment or components.
bullets: Data sheets come with individual accessories or components and give load capacity, component rating, IP rating, physical dimensions, etc.
Installation instructions cover how to physically install or fit the item, wiring/connection diagrams and, where relevant, programming instructions.
Product warranty information is often included in the instruction sheet or manual.
Catalogues show the type and range produced by a manufacturer; they are usually quite general, though some include technical data.
All manufacturers' catalogues are available on-line, but prices may not be included, to conceal the trade price.

sections.heading: The client's needs
paragraphs: The client or customer produces a general statement of what they require. They will normally appoint an architect or consultant to produce a more detailed plan for approval.
Once approved by the client (and approving authority), the customer's agent draws up detailed plans and specifications.

quiz.q: Why are detailed specifications, drawings and diagrams produced before work is tendered?
options: To enable contractors to tender for the work
To avoid the need for manufacturers' data
To remove the client's approval stage
quiz.why: They allow contractors to tender, with everyone pricing from the same base.

quiz.q: Which item typically gives load capacity, IP rating and physical dimensions of a component?
quiz.why: Data sheets normally provided with components contain load capacity, rating, IP rating and dimensions.

quiz.q: Which manufacturer document would contain wiring/connection diagrams and programming instructions?
quiz.why: Installation instructions cover fitting, wiring/connection diagrams and, where relevant, programming instructions.

quiz.q: Why might an on-line manufacturer's catalogue omit prices?
options: Prices are set by the architect
quiz.why: Prices may not be included in on-line catalogues, to conceal the trade price.

quiz.q: Who normally produces the more detailed plan from the client's general statement of requirements?
quiz.why: The client will normally appoint an architect or consultant to produce a more detailed plan for approval.

options: Equipment to be installed, where it goes and sizes
Only the price of the work
quiz.why: They give complete details including plans, equipment, locations and sizes.
